translations.text: And the word of the Lord came to Jonah son of Amittai, and said:
Arise and go to Nineveh, the great city, and preach in it, for the cry of its wickedness has risen up and is coming to me.

And Jonah arose to flee and go to Tarshish from the presence of the Lord. And he went down to Joppa and found a ship going to Tarshish, and he paid his fare, and went aboard it to go with them to Tarshish from the presence of the Lord.
And the Lord raised up a great wind upon the sea, and there was a great storm on the sea, and the ship was close to breaking apart.

And the sailors were afraid, and each man cried out to his own god, and they threw the cargo out of the ship into the sea to lighten it for them. But Jonah had gone down into the hold of the ship, and he was asleep and snoring.
And the ship's captain came to him and said to him: Why are you snoring? Arise and call upon your God; perhaps God will save us, and we will not perish.
And each man said to his companion: Come, let us cast lots and find out why this evil has come upon us. And they cast lots, and the lot fell on Jonah.
And they said to him: Tell us, what is your business, and where do you come from? Or from what country, or from what people are you?
And Jonah said to them: I am a servant of the Lord, and I fear and serve the Lord God of heaven, who made the sea and the dry land.

And the men were afraid with exceedingly great fear, and said to him: What is this that you have done? For the men understood that he was fleeing from the presence of the Lord, because he had told them.
And they said to him: What shall we do with you, so that this sea will calm down for us? For the sea was rising and stirring up its waves still more.
And Jonah said to them: Take me up and throw me into the sea, and the sea will calm down for you, for I know that this great storm is upon you because of me.
And the men strove with the ship to turn it back toward land, and they could not, for the sea kept coming on and rising higher against them.
And they cried out to the Lord and said: By no means, O Lord, let us not perish for the life of this man, and do not lay innocent blood upon us; for you, O Lord, have done as you willed.
And they took up Jonah and threw him into the sea, and the sea ceased from its raging.
And the men feared the Lord with exceedingly great fear, and they offered a sacrifice to God and made vows.
And the Lord commanded a great whale to swallow Jonah, and Jonah was in the belly of the whale three days and three nights.
And Jonah prayed to the Lord his God from within the belly of the whale.
And he said: In my affliction I cried out to the Lord my God, and he heard me; from the belly of hell, you heard the voice of my cry.
You cast me into the depths, into the heart of the sea, and rivers surrounded me. All your surges and your waves passed over me.
And I said: Have I been cast out from the sight of your eyes? Shall I ever again look upon your holy temple?
The waters poured over me up to my very soul, and the uttermost abyss surrounded me. My head went down into the clefts of the mountains.
I went down into the earth, whose bars are like everlasting bolts; and let my life come up from corruption to you, O Lord my God.
When my soul was failing within me, I remembered the Lord. Let my prayer come in before you, into your holy temple.
Those who hold to lawlessness and falsehood have forsaken their mercy.
But I will offer sacrifice to you with a voice of praise and confession. Whatever I have vowed I will give to you for my salvation, O Lord.
And the Lord commanded the sea monster, and it cast Jonah out onto dry land.
And the word of the Lord came to Jonah a second time, and said:
"Arise and go to Nineveh, that great city, and preach in it the same message as before, which I told you."
And Jonah arose and went to Nineveh, as the Lord had told him. Now Nineveh was a great city of God, so large that it took three days to walk across it.
And Jonah began to go into the city, about one day's journey, and began to preach, and said: "Three more days, and Nineveh will be overthrown."
And the people of Nineveh believed God. They proclaimed a fast and put on sackcloth, from the least of them to the greatest.
And this word reached the king of the Ninevites. He rose from his throne, took off his robe, put on sackcloth, and sat down on ashes.
And a proclamation was made and spoken in Nineveh by the king and by his nobles, and they said: "People and animals, cattle and sheep, do not taste anything. Do not graze, and do not drink water."
And people and animals put on sackcloth, and they cried out to God together. Each one turned back from his evil way and from the falsehood of their hands, and they said:
"Who knows? God may repent and turn back from the anger of his wrath, and we will not perish."
And God saw their deeds, that they had turned back from their evil deeds. And God repented of the evil which he had said he would do to them, and he did not do it.
And Jonah was grieved with great grief, and was troubled.

He prayed to the Lord and said: "O Lord, were these not my words while I was still in my own land? That is why I hurried to flee to Tarshish, for I know that you are merciful and compassionate, long-suffering and abundant in mercy, and that you repent of doing evil.
And now, Lord, take my soul from me, for my death is better than my life."
And the Lord said to Jonah, "Are you greatly grieved?" And Jonah said, "I am greatly grieved, even to the point of death."
And Jonah went out of the city and sat down facing the city. He made himself a booth there and sat under it in the shade, until he could see what [?] would happen to the city.

And the Lord God commanded a gourd plant, and it sprang up over Jonah's head, to be a shade over Jonah's head and to shade him from that evil heat. And Jonah rejoiced over the gourd plant with very great joy.
And at dawn the next day God commanded a worm, and it struck the gourd plant, and it withered.

And when the sun rose, God commanded a hot, scorching wind, and the sun beat down on Jonah's head. He grew faint, and his soul was leaving him, and he said: "Death is better for me than this life of mine."
And the Lord God said to Jonah, "Are you greatly grieved because of that gourd plant?" And Jonah said, "I am greatly grieved, even to the point of death."
And the Lord said to Jonah: "You are concerned about the gourd and have pity on it, though you did not labor over it or make it grow. It sprang up in a night, and in a night it perished.
Should I not spare Nineveh, this great city, in which live more than twelve myriads (120,000) of people who do not know their right hand from their left, and also a great many cattle?"
